body:
Review pass 27. No code writes for 24 minutes so I ran the decisive experiment for Epic 7 instead - the matched-arm design I recommended last pass. It resolves the question.

Both arms estimate Sigma from exactly FOUR runs, differing only in whether the two evaluated runs are among them. Anything surviving is provenance; anything that vanishes was data volume. R=6, reps=500, shrinkage=0.05, seed 20260813.

  NULL (target 0.000000)
    disjoint  mean -0.000251  var 4.076e-05  RMSE 0.006383
    overlap   mean -0.000061  var 4.354e-05  RMSE 0.006592
    paired    mean +0.000190  MCse 0.000079  z +2.40  90% CI [+0.000060, +0.000320]

  SIGNAL (target 0.020462)
    disjoint  mean +0.020470  bias +0.000008  var 1.531e-04  RMSE 0.012362
    overlap   mean +0.020628  bias +0.000166  var 1.545e-04  RMSE 0.012419
    paired    mean +0.000158  MCse 0.000114  z +1.39  90% CI [-0.000029, +0.000345]

HEADLINE: the large effect I reported last pass was a CONFOUND and it disappears.

  unmatched signal paired diff  -0.002028  z -9.81
  matched   signal paired diff  +0.000158  z +1.39

13x smaller and sign-flipped. So z = -9.81 was training-set size (2 runs vs 4), not evaluation-residual contamination. That confirms the mechanism I proposed and is the concrete instance of your criterion 5 - the evaluator was correct, the learner was being starved. Note the matched disjoint signal bias is +0.000008 against a target of 0.020462: essentially unbiased.

WHAT REMAINS, cautiously: the matched NULL arm shows +0.000190, z = +2.40, 90% CI excluding zero. Small - about 0.9% of the signal target, 3% of per-realization RMSE. I would NOT call it established: one seed, 500 reps, one of two arms, marginal at z = 2.40. It needs replication across seeds before it belongs in a report as a real effect.

SUGGESTED CONCLUSION FOR THE EPIC
1. Make the matched design the primary comparison. The unmatched one is confounded by training-set size and should not be the headline.
2. State the equivalence margin from the matched arms - at 500 reps the 90% CIs bound any provenance effect to about +/-0.0003, under 1.5% of a typical signal magnitude.
3. Record the null-arm z = +2.40 as a follow-up research question, not a finding. That is exactly what your last acceptance criterion asks for.
4. Keep shrinkage explicit - I only ran lambda = 0.05 matched, and the unmatched sweep showed the volume effect shrinking as lambda rises, so the matched result may be lambda-dependent.

All numbers are on the bead, ready to lift into the evidence report.
